          Vertical, Relentless, Effective: The Tottenham Transformation Under Martin Ho
        
      
                          
                      Sep 23, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Martin Ho has overseen a remarkable turnaround at Tottenham. From an 11th-place finish two seasons ago to one of the WSL's most exciting and progressive teams, and just one of four unbeaten sides this season after three games. How close are Spurs to closing the gap on the division's elite?

Tottenham Hotspur's 7-0 victory over Crystal Palace may have been the performance that turned heads in the Women's Super League this weekend, but the foundations for such a display have been building for some time.

Just over a year ago, Spurs were coming off an 11th-place finish and searching for a new direction. While there had been flashes of progress in earlier seasons, including fifth- and sixth place finishes in 2021-22 and 2023-24 respectively, their slide towards the bottom end of the table in 2024-25 underlined the gap that still existed to the league's leading clubs.
Since Martin Ho's arrival in July 2025, however, that trajectory has changed dramatically.

Tottenham collected a club-record 36 WSL points in Ho's first season in charge, winning 11 matches and returning to fifth place. Indeed, that points tally was the most ever by an English manager in their debut season in the competition.
Since taking the reins, Ho has overseen 13 WSL victories in just 25 matches, with only Manchester City (21), Chelsea (17) and Arsenal (16) winning more games in that period.
And their start to the 2026-27 campaign suggests that progress has continued.
Spurs are one of only four unbeaten teams remaining in the division, and sit second in the table after three matches, just behind Man City.

Tottenham are currently enjoying a six-match unbeaten run in the competition, equalling the longest in the club's WSL history, and the first since such a six-game streak between October-November 2023. The challenge now is sustaining that momentum.
They face the third-toughest fixture run in the division over their next five WSL games according to the Opta Power Rankings, coming up against London City Lionesses, Chelsea and Arsenal.
That makes their start even more intriguing.

Spurs won four of their opening five WSL games last season, before winning just seven of their remaining 17. This time around, Ho will be hoping his side can bridge that gap to the league’s elite, and, crucially, sustain their strong start across the entirety of the campaign.
The meetings with the ‘big four' will provide a significant test, but there is growing evidence that Spurs are closer to that level than they have been before.
Ho's emphasis on brave, front-foot football combined with defensive discipline is already evident in Tottenham's early-season performances, none more so than their 7-0 victory over Crystal Palace.

While the visitors were helped by Palace being reduced to 10 players after just seven minutes, scoring seven goals at WSL level is no simple task. After all, this was a Palace side that had drawn 0-0 against Arsenal at Emirates Stadium just a week earlier despite facing 30 shots.
The manner of Tottenham's dominance was particularly striking. Spurs registered 42 shots, the third-highest total in WSL history, and the most ever recorded by an away side in the competition.

They also amassed 82 touches in the opposition box, the most by Tottenham in a WSL match and the joint fourth-highest total ever recorded in the league. No team had reached that figure since Chelsea managed 82 against Leicester City in December 2024.
On top of that, the game was goalless at the break, with all seven goals coming in a ruthless second half.

There were standout individual performances.Olivia Holdt became just the second Tottenham player to score a WSL hat-trick, after Martha Thomas against Aston Villa in October 2023, while Amanda Nildén‘s late goal perfectly captured the collective nature of Spurs' attacking play.
Nildén's 86th-minute strike came at the end of a 37-second move involving nine different Tottenham players, the most players involved in a single WSL goal this season.

          UEFA Women's Champions League Predictions 2026-27: The Opta Supercomputer Projections
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Yash Thakur / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Who will win the UEFA Women's Champions League in 2026-27? Will Barcelona retain their crown? Here, we detail how the Opta supercomputer sees this season playing out.
The UEFA Women’s Champions League is back with its 18-team league-phase format for the 2026-27 season, and Matchday 1 kicks off on Tuesday.

Each team will play six games in the league phase, with the top four teams at the end securing direct qualification to the quarter-finals, while the teams ranked 5th to 12th will compete in a knockout play-off to book their place in the last eight.

Barcelona were crowned champions for the fourth time in their history after thrashing OL Lyonnes 4-0 in the final last season. Ewa Pajor and Salma Paralluelo both scored twice in the second half to secure the title.

In a summer of major moves, two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas departed Barcelona for the WSL, while Salma Paralluelo made the switch to Lyon. Arsenal and Lyon have both strengthened their already potent attacks, Real Madrid continue to build around an exciting young core, and Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Manchester City will all be firmly in the hunt for silverware this season.
So, which side has got the Opta supercomputer's backing for European glory?

Barcelona come into another season as the favourites to win the competition and equal their men’s team’s tally of five European titles. The Spanish champions have featured in all the UWCL finals this decade, being crowned champions four times.

Despite losing some long serving members of the squad this summer, Pere Romeu’s side came out winners in 41.2% of the supercomputer's simulations. The Blaugranas are the side to beat in Europe and have lost just three out of 38 games in the UWCL since the start of 2023, with all three losses coming against English sides (1-0 vs Arsenal on 24 May 2025, 2-0 vs Man City on 10 October 2024 and 1-0 vs Chelsea on 20 April 2024).

After losing out to eventual champions Barcelona in the semi-finals of the last edition, Bayern Munich are the second most likely side to win the competition this season with Opta’s supercomputer. José Barcala’s winning machine reached the final in 34.8% of the simulations and were crowned champions in 17.3% of them.

In fact, Bayern’s only two losses in all competitions last season came at the hands of Barcelona (7-1 in October and 4-2 in May). Although Georgia Stanway switched the Bavarians for Arsenal this summer, Barcala should feel confident in their attack of Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder, Edna Imade and others.
Bayern and Barça are set to face each other again in the final match of the league phase this season. Bayern will hope to do better this time.
According to the supercomputer, all English teams and OL Lyonnes are expected to secure a place in the quarter-finals of the UWCL this year, alongside the title contenders of course.

Sonia Bompastor’s Chelsea (94.0%) have been given the second highest chance of reaching the last eight of the competition, behind Barcelona. This is largely down to their favourable draw as the Blues have the lowest average fixture difficulty rating of all teams in the league phase this year.

Surprisingly, the Opta supercomputer is not too bullish on the prospects of eight-time champions and last year’s runners-up OL Lyonnes, or the 2024-25 champions Arsenal. Those two teams came out on top in only 8.7% and 7.0% of the simulations, respectively.Jonatan Giráldez's side reached the final in 20.6% of simulations, behind Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Chelsea and Man City. Despite adding more attacking firepower to the side with the signings of Caroline Weir and Paralluelo, Lyon lack balance in the midfield following Lindsey Heaps’ departure this summer to Denver Summit FC.
The side struggled to maintain the intensity and compactness throughout the 90 minutes in last season’s final against Barcelona and could yet fall short in that regard this season.

Renee Slegers’ Arsenal have had their own issues in front of goal, unable to maximise their goalscoring opportunities, a glimpse of what has continuously haunted the Gunners when it comes to the fine margins.

Their recent goalless draw against Crystal Palace was another in a long list of games where they failed to convert their chances. According to the Opta supercomputer, Arsenal reached the final on just 17.8% of the simulations.

English champions Manchester City reached the semi-final stage in 50.1% of the simulations on their return to the competition. Andree Jeglertz’s side haven’t featured in the final four since the 2017-18 season, when they were beaten by the eventual champions Lyon thanks to a goal by Lucy Bronze.

Spearheaded by Khadija Shaw, City will hope to add a European star to their domestic triumphs, building on their momentum. The side has talented players across all positions but potentially lacks the depth needed to compete three times a week.

Outside the top six, Real Madrid have the highest probability of making the quarter-finals of the UWCL this season (49.6%). Las Blancas have lost their leading goalscorer and assist provider in the club’s history, Caroline Weir, but have brought in the prodigious talent of Felicia Schroder to lead the attack alongside Linda Caicedo.

113zwiiotwzbp1qrrhyk053ne3.title: De Bruyne: I did not try to leave Napoli
113zwiiotwzbp1qrrhyk053ne3.subtitle: Kevin De Bruyne previously seemed to suggest he could leave Napoli, but the Belgian has insisted he did not try to do so this summer.
paragraphs: Kevin De Bruyne has claimed he did not attempt to push through an exit from Napoli in the summer transfer window.
De Bruyne previously suggested he was unhappy at Napoli, and there was speculation linking him with a move away from the Serie A club.
The Manchester City great did not see eye to eye with coach Antonio Conte, who has since been replaced by Massimiliano Allegri.
De Bruyne, however, has now insisted he was not interested in leaving Napoli.
He told reporters: "No, I haven't really spoken to anyone about it.
"I just enjoyed my holidays and went straight back to Naples."
Napoli have made their worst start to a Serie A season in a decade, having taken seven points from their opening five matches.
De Bruyne, though, is not overly concerned.
He said: "We've had a rough start to the season, we've played a lot of strong teams already.
"We even had the chance to win it in the final minute against Inter, but we still lost. Those details are the difference between our seven points and the 10 or 11 we might've deserved.
"We're not doing so well in terms of points, but I think we're doing fine."
Injury restricted De Bruyne to 21 games last term. He scored five goals, assisted four more and created 40 chances.
De Bruyne has made six appearances this season, scoring once and providing one assist.

11saz8tdl2qod1a8ck4tw8mtj9.title: Koge relishing Women's Champions League adventure after Arsenal edge out minnows
11saz8tdl2qod1a8ck4tw8mtj9.subtitle: Arsenal had 19 shots but hit the target just twice as they edged out minnows Koge in their opening Women's Champions League games.
paragraphs: Nadia Nadim says minnows Koge are simply relishing their Women's Champions League adventure following a narrow defeat to Arsenal.
The Gunners, European champions in 2025, clinched a 1-0 win over the Danish team, who are featuring in just their second Champions League campaign.
Mariona Caldentey's last-gasp penalty claimed the points for Arsenal, who were wasteful in front of goal.
Arsenal had 19 shots, but got just two of them on target, while they also hit the woodwork.
While Koge suffered late heartbreak, Nadim, who led the visitors' line, was thrilled with her team-mates.
"So proud of the team and the way we conducted ourselves, especially in the first half," she told ESPN on Disney+.

"We have a young team, a lot of them have no experience playing at this level, good for them to experience what it's like at this level. Good learning, disappointed they got the goal and penalty in the last minute. That's a part of the game, could've done better, but it's our first Champions League game and there's a lot of games left.
"We wanted to be compact and keep the ball, we had people who were comfortable with the ball. We changed in the last 30 minutes, and it didn't do us well because we couldn't get out of the pressure.
"Credit to Arsenal, great team, they find each other well. It's okay, happy for the young players to experience this.
"I enjoy the game. Physically, it's tough because you're so low, it becomes hard to be dangerous, takes a toll to try and get in the box the whole time.
"I love football, I love this game. It's nice to be back here. I always love the Champions League. Now we're a new team, let's see where this adventure will take us."
English sides are now unbeaten in their last 11 Champions League games against clubs from Denmark (W8 D3), since Arsenal’s 1-5 defeat to Fortuna Hjorring in the 2002-03 semi-final.
This win did see Arsenal snap a run of losing their opening Champions League fixtures in each of the past two seasons.
"We left it late," said Arsenal defender Steph Catley.
"It's tough at the moment and in the Champions League there are no easy games. They defended great, we didn't score early and it didn't come until the end.

"In the Champions League, you never think it's an easy day. I was expecting a tough game and it became really difficult but credit to the girls, they did everything and Mariona was very calm in that moment.

"It's hard to put your finger on it [what is going wrong], it is a bit of a slog and the goals are not coming as freely as they have in the past. It's not a lack of trying, we're doing everything we can to put the ball into the back of the net.

"We have great history in this competition and it's important we are in it every year and challenging to win. We have a real belief that we can go on and win it. It's a long season and we're working really hard so to get the wins early on is very important."
Elsewhere on Tuesday, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain drew 1-1.
Felicia Schroder opened the scoring for Madrid after just two minutes, but Sakina Karchaoui equalised from the penalty spot in the second half.

12wp6fcugs0qg1dmw9ecnwclom.title: Chelsea's Estevao to 'seize every opportunity' after falling behind Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro
12wp6fcugs0qg1dmw9ecnwclom.subtitle: Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have shone as a front three for Chelsea this season, with Estevao playing a backup role.
paragraphs: Estevao is determined to "seize every opportunity" he gets at Chelsea, having found himself behind Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro in Xabi Alonso's pecking order.
The Brazilian arrived at Stamford Bridge from Palmeiras in 2025 and appeared 36 times across all competitions for the Blues in his debut season at Stamford Bridge.

Across those outings, 20 of which were starts, he scored eight goals and laid on three assists, while ranking second for dribbles attempted (133) and third for dribbles completed (58) among all players in Chelsea's squad, despite his relative lack of gametime.

The 19-year-old would have been hoping to kick on at the start of 2026-27, following Xabi Alonso's appointment as head coach, but he is yet to provide a goal involvement in six outings and has only started twice.
While Pedro Neto has found a new role at wing-back in Alonso's 3-4-3 system, the attacking trio of Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro have been highly impressive.
Of the Blues' 10 Premier League goals this season, only one – Romeo Lavia's opening goal in a 4-3 win over Brighton – has not involved at least one of that trio as the scorer or the assister.
Estevao understands the form of Chelsea's other attackers has limited his opportunities, but he hopes to make a big impression when he gets a chance.
"I think every coach has their own way of playing. Of course, we work every day, I give my best every day, and that's what I do," Estevao said at a press conference while on international duty.
"We have quality players at Chelsea, so what I do is focus on what I can control. I try to give my best in training. When I get an opportunity, I try to give my best, day after day.
"I try to seize every opportunity I have, control everything I can, and I leave it in God's hands, and I trust myself a lot, too."
Estevao has only played 148 minutes in all competitions for Chelsea this term, compared to 578 for Palmer and 552 for Rogers, with those figures making them the Blues' two most-used players.
Joao Pedro has played 377 minutes, having missed last Friday's 3-0 defeat to Brentford due to a knee issue.
That injury caused the striker to withdraw from Brazil's squad, but Estevao will hope to rack up some minutes when the Selecao face Australia (twice) and India in friendlies.

Across those outings, 20 of which were starts, he scored eight goals and laid on three assists, while ranking second for dribbles attempted (133) and third for dribbles completed (58) among all players in Chelsea's squad, despite his relative lack of gametime. 

The 19-year-old would have been hoping to kick on at the start of 2026-27, following Xabi Alonso's appointment as head coach, but he is yet to provide a goal involvement in six outings and has only started twice.

While Pedro Neto has found a new role at wing-back in Alonso's 3-4-3 system, the attacking trio of Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro have been highly impressive.

Of the Blues' 10 Premier League goals this season, only one – Romeo Lavia's opening goal in a 4-3 win over Brighton – has not involved at least one of that trio as the scorer or the assister.

Estevao understands the form of Chelsea's other attackers has limited his opportunities, but he hopes to make a big impression when he gets a chance. 

"I think every coach has their own way of playing. Of course, we work every day, I give my best every day, and that's what I do," Estevao said at a press conference while on international duty.

"We have quality players at Chelsea, so what I do is focus on what I can control. I try to give my best in training. When I get an opportunity, I try to give my best, day after day.

"I try to seize every opportunity I have, control everything I can, and I leave it in God's hands, and I trust myself a lot, too."

Estevao has only played 148 minutes in all competitions for Chelsea this term, compared to 578 for Palmer and 552 for Rogers, with those figures making them the Blues' two most-used players. 

Joao Pedro has played 377 minutes, having missed last Friday's 3-0 defeat to Brentford due to a knee issue.

That injury caused the striker to withdraw from Brazil's squad, but Estevao will hope to rack up some minutes when the Selecao face Australia (twice) and India in friendlies.

18kaq92nmwrzf1g1gvjiraypwh.title: Ter Stegen says Klopp call-up was extra special following injury woes
18kaq92nmwrzf1g1gvjiraypwh.subtitle: Marc-Andre ter Stegen has already been named as Jurgen Klopp's Germany number one, after more than a year in the international wilderness.
paragraphs: Marc-Andre ter Stegen says being named as Jurgen Klopp's first-choice goalkeeper for Germany was extra special, following his well-documented injury issues.

Germany will face the Netherlands in their first match under Klopp on Thursday, in the Nations League, with further games against Greece (home and away) and Serbia to come during this international break.
And, with Manuel Neuer retiring from international football in the aftermath of Germany's shock round-of-32 World Cup defeat to Paraguay, the former Liverpool boss had to name a new number one.
Despite calling up Besiktas' Alexander Nubel, Bayern Munich's Jonas Urbig, Eintracht Frankfurt's Noah Atubolu and Augsburg's Finn Dahmen, he has gone with the experience of Ter Stegen.
The most recent of Ter Stegen's 44 caps came against France in the previous edition of the Nations League in June 2025, with injuries restricting his gametime in recent years.
He only made 10 appearances across all competitions combined in 2024-25 and 2025-26, for parent club Barcelona and Girona, who he joined on loan for the second half of last season.
But, after starting eight straight games for his latest loan club, Ajax, Ter Stegen is excited to be back on the international stage.

"It's always something special for me, to be here again now," he told Sky Sport DE. "Especially if you had a time when things didn't go the way you imagined, when your body wasn't by your side, then of course, you appreciate it all the more.

"I believe that I have worked a lot to make this happen again. I'm also looking forward to meeting many new faces, some old friends who are here, and just to start again and give our best for the team.
"There's a smile on my face. I'm just happy to be 100% back, to be able to be with the national team and hopefully play successful football. That is the wish of all of us."

Klopp takes charge of his country after overseeing 674 games in the Bundesliga and the Premier League, across wildly successful spells with Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool. That is more games in Europe's top five leagues than any previous Germany head coach had tallied before taking the job.
Ter Stegen said of Klopp: "He's one of one, as you know, with the joy he conveys and his interest in football, the enthusiasm he has for his own football.
"I don't think you need to say anything. I think everyone knows him and everyone knows how much he lives and feels football."

Klopp is one of only three bosses – alongside Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti – to have won the Bundesliga and Premier League titles, and he became famed for his "heavy metal" style of play with both Dortmund and Liverpool.

But Ter Stegen knows adopting that way of playing will be a learning curve for Germany, adding: "There are issues he would like to tackle, because he has his way of seeing football and understanding football. We have to try to internalise that as quickly as possible.

"For the time being, there are smaller levers that can and must be pulled, to then get into his philosophy. We want to play great football from the start, to defend not through individual actions, but really through the collective.
"We have very few training sessions to talk a lot about gameplan and so on, so we will keep it relatively simple now. We have to be attentive and implement that as quickly as possible."

18kqj4ll7crqczd8mfxkvej68.title: Branthwaite hopes injury issues are behind him following England recall
18kqj4ll7crqczd8mfxkvej68.subtitle: Injuries have restricted Jarrad Branthwaite to just one senior cap for England, but he will hope to add to that tally in the next two weeks.
paragraphs: Jarrad Branthwaite hopes he is back in the England setup for good after missing Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup, having earned a recall to the Three Lions' squad.
Branthwaite has been named in Thomas Tuchel's group for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia (who they face both home and away) and Croatia.

He has been an ever-present for Everton so far this season, helping the Toffees keep three clean sheets in five games and concede the joint-fewest goals in the Premier League (three, alongside Leeds United).

Branthwaite won his only senior England cap to date in June 2024, when he was named in Gareth Southgate's preliminary Euro 2024 squad and appeared in a friendly against Bosnia-Herzegovina, only to miss out on the final party.
The 24-year-old also missed this summer's World Cup after an injury-hit 2025-26 season, in which he was restricted to just 10 Premier League appearances and seven starts.

But, having visited a specialist in Germany in a bid to combat his persistent hamstring issues during the off-season, Branthwaite hopes he can now challenge Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa for an England starting spot.
"Being out for such a long time with injury didn't help, missing three or four of the camps and missing a lot of football," Branthwaite said of his England struggles.
"My aim is to stay injury-free and play as many games as I can and keep giving myself the best possible chance to be in the squad.
"I've not spoken to him [Tuchel] recently. When we get there, we'll have a chat. I can't wait to join up with the squad and enjoy the couple of weeks.

"It is a proud moment. In the last season or so, it has been a target of mine when I've been out to get back playing and give myself the best possible chance of being in and around the England squad after missing a length of time.
"The season has started well individually and as a team and that has definitely helped. I believe I am good enough to be in the England squad, so hopefully I can show that."

Branthwaite, Guehi, Konsa, Jarell Quansah and Trevoh Chalobah are the centre-backs in England's group for this international break, with their Nations League opener against world champions Spain taking place at Wembley on Saturday.
England have won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of their last five without conceding.
Only once before have the Three Lions won six competitive home fixtures to nil, doing so between March 2015 and March 2017.
However, Spain are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest ever streak by a European nation.

194kvzunupcho1w6yo91gg0suu.title: Bompastor will not risk James in Champions League as Arsenal clash looms
194kvzunupcho1w6yo91gg0suu.subtitle: Chelsea open their Women's Champions League campaign against Austria Wien, but with Arsenal next up in the WSL, squad rotation is likely.
paragraphs: Chelsea will not take any risks with Lauren James against Austria Wien in the Women's Champions League, as Sonia Bompastor looks to get her ready to face Arsenal on Sunday.

The Blues are overwhelming favourites to open their European league-phase campaign with three points on Wednesday, with the Opta supercomputer assigning them a 93.3% chance of victory over the tournament debutants.
Chelsea's only previous meeting with an Austrian side in the Champions League came last season, as they thumped St. Polten 6-0 in the league phase.
Having gone out at the quarter-final stage last term following three straight semi-final defeats, the Blues are hoping to go further in Europe this term, but rotation is likely this week.
With a huge London derby against Arsenal on the horizon in the Women's Super League, Bompastor has already confirmed James – who picked up a minor injury in training – will be rested.
"She should be available for the game on the weekend, but we don't want to take any risks for the game tomorrow," Bompastor said of James. "She's a bit short."
Bompastor also confirmed Erin Cuthbert, Manaka Matsukubo and Aggie Beever-Jones are all back in training, with the latter being the only one of that trio to appear in a WSL match this season.
"They are training again with the team, so a lot of players and it's good news. Manaka is back in training, not fully fit yet, but it's good to have her back," Bompastor said.
"It's really good to see Erin back. I'm always happy when I have most of my players on the pitch. It brings positivity around the team and the quality on the pitch progresses.
"It's always good to have that competition in the squad, with everyone happy to be on the pitch together."
Chelsea lost just one of their eight games in the Champions League last season (W5 D2), conceding the fewest goals of any side in the competition (six).

Austria Wien will become the fourth different side from Austria to participate in the Champions League, but those teams are winless in 21 games in the competition (D3 L18) since St. Polten beat Slavia Prague 1-0 in November 2022.
English sides have won all five of their meetings with Austrian opponents in the competition by an aggregate score of 17-2.

1b1jzurh3d3i4144cnru6aexc4.title: Real Madrid 'living in another galaxy' over referee claims, says LaLiga chief Tebas
1b1jzurh3d3i4144cnru6aexc4.subtitle: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has slammed Real Madrid for their treatment of referee Ortiz Arias following Sunday's loss to Atletico Madrid.
paragraphs: Real Madrid are "living in another galaxy" if they believe LaLiga's officials are biased against them, the competition's president Javier Tebas said amid a fierce debate over refereeing standards.
Madrid were beaten 2-1 by Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby at the Estadio Metropolitano, but the controversial nature of their loss sparked a furious reaction from Los Blancos.

Jose Mourinho's team had Dean Huijsen sent off for a last-man foul early in the second half, but Madrid felt Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have seen red for Atleti, the former for a high challenge on Federico Valverde and the latter for treading on Jude Bellingham.
Mourinho brought printed images of both incidents to his post-match press conference, saying they were the "story of the game" and describing referee Ortiz Arias as weak and inexperienced.
Atleti hit back on their social media channels on Monday, posting an image taken during Mourinho's press conference alongside the caption: "Stop referee harassment now."
Madrid used the title "a terrible refereeing performance decides the derby" for their official club-produced match report, accompanied by images of the Lee and Romero challenges.
And Tebas – who has criticised Madrid's treatment of referees and desire to set up a breakaway European Super League in the past – has now slammed the club's behaviour.

"Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime's television, building the same old narrative: the permanent conspiracy," Tebas wrote on X, responding to a Spanish media article that alleged referees routinely favour Madrid's opponents.
"Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy.
"That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.
"It's more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what's happening on the pitch.
"GET THE BLINDERS OFF! It's September, and they're already claiming the League is tainted. Nobody with common sense believes that old excuse anymore."

Madrid previously sent a formal letter of complaint about LaLiga's referees to the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) in 2025, prompting Tebas to accuse Madrid of harming the competition and "building a story of victimhood."

1fzdvkfezt9fe1nqwb3atnr56w.title: Mbappe: Working under Zidane 'like something from a movie'
1fzdvkfezt9fe1nqwb3atnr56w.subtitle: Current Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe will link up with former Blancos hero Zinedine Zidane for the first time this week, with France.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has likened being coached by Zinedine Zidane to "something from a movie", as France prepare to play their first game under the legendary former midfielder.
Zidane succeeded Didier Deschamps in the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup, which saw France reach the semi-finals before losing 2-0 to eventual champions Spain.

Deschamps led Les Bleus for 14 years and 187 matches in total (also 103 as a player), overseeing their second World Cup triumph in 2018 in addition to runner-up finishes at the 2022 edition and at Euro 2016, with the latter tournament being on home soil.
And France's new era begins with a Nations League trip to Turkiye on Friday, with matches against Belgium – both home and away – and Italy to follow in the next two weeks.
Zidane made 108 appearances for France during his illustrious playing career, scoring 31 goals including a brace in their win over Brazil in the 1998 World Cup final.
He also scored a Panenka penalty in the 2006 final before receiving a red card for an infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi, as Italy went on to defeat Les Bleus on spot-kicks.
And Mbappe – who will keep hold of the captain's armband under the new regime – has a chance to pass Zidane in the all-time France appearance charts during the extended international break.
Mbappe's next cap will be his 107th, so he could potentially equal Zidane against Belgium next Monday and surpass him versus Italy on October 2, should he appear in all of those matches.

In an interview with AS, Mbappe recalled his first meeting with Zidane, which came when he was a youth player attracting interest from Europe's top clubs, while the former midfield icon was working in Real Madrid's academy.
"Years ago, he was the first to pick me up ‌and ⁠take me to Real Madrid, to the training complex. I was 13 or 14; it was ages ago," Mbappe said.
"And now he's my national team coach. It's like something from a movie, but he's top-level.
"It's real, we're in a new process in France, we have two years to prepare for the European Championships and we're working towards it now."

Zidane is the only manager to win three successive Champions League crowns, doing so with Real Madrid between 2015-16 and 2017-18, but he neglected to take another job in club football after leaving the Santiago Bernabeu for the second time in 2021.
He repeatedly outlined his interest in the France job during the latter years of Deschamps' tenure, and Mbappe is excited to see what changes he makes.
"It's a new phase with a new coach. It's going ⁠to be a new experience for everyone, since we've only ever had Deschamps," Mbappe said.
"It will be a change for us, but I think ⁠everything will turn out very well."

1gbxvraddlm741a2vdd005k0y5.title: Slegers: Big Arsenal squad is a 'luxury problem'
1gbxvraddlm741a2vdd005k0y5.subtitle: Renee Slegers is prepared to rotate her Arsenal squad ahead of their Women's Champions League opener against Koge.
paragraphs: Renee Slegers believes having a large squad is a "luxury problem" as Arsenal prepare for their Women's Champions League opener against Koge.
Arsenal won the Champions League in 2024-25 but fell at the semi-final hurdle last season, as Lyon came from behind to beat them on aggregate and reach the showpiece.
The Gunners, who also finished as runners-up to Manchester City in the Women's Super League last term, bolstered their squad over the summer as they aim to fight for silverware once again.

They brought in eight new signings, including Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodriguez, but so far, it has not had the desired effect, with Arsenal winning just one of their three WSL games (D2).
Slegers' side have a big week ahead of them, with a WSL clash with Chelsea to come after their Champions League outing.
But Slegers pointed out that Arsenal were prepared for their packed schedule.
"It's a luxury problem, of course," Slegers said when asked if a big squad was a nice problem to have.
"We have so many different options. The balance becomes, or the challenge becomes, how do you then choose certain things for certain games?
"We're still keeping the main ideas and consistency within the team. You don't chop and change everything.
"At the same time, if I look at where the players are at and where we are, from a game model understanding and players playing their roles, it's on a really high level throughout the squad.
"That also makes me really confident to say, 'I can make changes. These partnerships are working. This is working. This player knows her role on the pitch'.
"It's in a really good place, and that's where we wanted it to be. For the length of the season and all the games that we're going to play, we are able to do these things.

"The reason why we have the size of the squad with basically only senior national team players, so much quality doubled up in every position, is that we can use the whole squad. Especially when it's short turnarounds and we need freshness."
Arsenal are heavy favourites to beat Koge, with an 81.1% win probability according to the Opta supercomputer.
They have won both of their previous meetings with Koge in the Champions League, beating them twice in the 2021-22 group stage (3-0 home, 5-1 away).
However, Arsenal have lost their opening game in each of the last two Champions League seasons: 2-5 to Bayern Munich in 2024-25 and 1-2 to Lyon in 2025-26.
Slegers is also familiar with Koge herself, having faced them while in charge of Rosengard, and she is expecting a tough challenge.

1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.title: Carrick understands jeers from Man Utd fans after Mainoo substitution
1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.subtitle: Manchester United's travelling fans made their feelings known when Kobbie Mainoo was substituted with 10 minutes to play against Fulham.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick understands the "emotional" reactions to Manchester United's recent struggles, after his decision to withdraw Kobbie Mainoo against Fulham was booed by their travelling fans.
With just five points on the board after five games, United have made their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign, having also taken five at this stage of 2014-15.

Things could have been worse for the Red Devils at Craven Cottage on Sunday, too, as Matheus Cunha's deflected strike snatched a point in the 89th minute, after Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal had put them on the back foot.
With United 1-0 down and chasing the game, Carrick's choice to replace Mainoo with Mason Mount in the 80th minute was loudly jeered by the away end.
Mainoo had completed 64 of his 68 passes, 27 of which were in the final third, with only Bryan Mbeumo (100%) and Harry Maguire (95.8%) bettering his 94.1% pass accuracy among United's starters.
But Carrick feels that reaction came from a place of frustration and understands the disgruntled feeling among the fanbase.
"There are always going to be certain reactions when you're making changes," Carrick said. "I've spoken to Kobbie after the game and he's absolutely fine.
"I understand at times when we are chasing the game, everyone's a little bit emotional. The supporters are – as they should be – desperate for us to do the right thing.
"But I don't take any negatives or offence to it. I think we've just got to try and keep doing the right things to get back into the game.
"The supporters were unbelievable, I have to say, all the way through. They stuck with the boys and supported them.
"At least we've given them something small at the end to take from it, and I'm sure there's more to come."

With United 12th in the Premier League table going into the extended international break, the Opta supercomputer only assigns them a 17% chance of qualifying for the Champions League, but Carrick is sure there are plenty of twists and turns ahead.
"It's still a big season ahead," Carrick said. "It's a long season, and you're going to have these spells through a season. That's part of the journey. It's not a sprint; it's a long effort.
"I'm not playing it down. We wanted more points, so I'm not saying everything's great. I understand the frustration. We wanted to be better, and we wanted to do other things.
"But deflation is certainly not what we have within the club and within the group. The players didn't have that on the pitch, and that's what will carry us through the season, without a doubt."
United face Tottenham, who are still winless and prop up the table, in their next Premier League game on October 10.

1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.title: Amorim vows not to repeat Man Utd errors with Milan
1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.subtitle: AC Milan's unbeaten start in Serie A under Ruben Amorim rolled on, and he intends to continue allowing his team to play with freedom.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim insists he will not be pushed into making the same tactical mistakes he made during his stint with Manchester United, now he is in charge of AC Milan.
Amorim's unbeaten start in Serie A continued on Sunday with a comfortable 3-0 win against Lecce at San Siro, with the result moving Milan up to fifth in the standings.
Christian Pulisic's sensational touch and finish put Milan ahead early on, before Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira sealed the win for the Rossoneri during a dominant second half.
Milan's victory saw them remain unbeaten in their opening five Serie A matches of a season for the first time since 2022-23 (W3 D2).

Amorim (W3 D2) has become only the third foreign manager in Milan's history to not taste defeat in each of his first five Serie A games in charge, after Luis Carniglia (W3 D2) and Nils Liedholm (W4 D1), both in 1963-64.

Speaking after the game, Amorim revealed he allowed his side to play with "freedom", and when asked about the reasoning behind that decision, he highlighted his turbulent tenure at Old Trafford, where he was reluctant to adapt his style of play.
"It's an observation of the games and the characteristics," Amorim told DAZN, as quoted by Football Italia.

"Of course, I listen to the players, but a manager, especially in a big team, is always listening to the players, seeing and understanding them, but every player wants to push the game towards their characteristics, and if you want to have an identity, that is hard.
"It's always my decision. What I felt in the last games is the same that I felt at Manchester United, and I cannot make the same mistake.
"Sometimes we don't have the perfect characteristics to play in that way, and if we don't have them, we have to adapt. I think today worked.
"In another game, we can return to the build-up with three [at the back]. The important thing is to have different ways of playing.

"That's especially important in Italy, because the managers are really smart, they mark really well one against one, and when they lose the reference to what we want to do, it's harder for them to understand their mobility, just as they make it harder for me to understand their teams."

Milan have now won their first two home Serie A matches of a season while keeping a clean sheet in both for the first time since 2020-21, when they beat Bologna 2-0 and Spezia 3-0 under Stefano Pioli.

Their dominance was backed up by the underlying metrics, too. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.93 from their 10 attempts, while also restricting Lecce to a measly xG total of 0.17 from six shots.
It was a much-needed victory heading into the international break, with Milan coming into the clash with Lecce without a win in three matches in all competitions (D2 L1).
Roma, Inter and Lazio are the early pace setters in the division, all sitting two points clear of Milan, and Amorim feels his team are on the right track.
"If you look at the way we play, Roma and Inter had more time as a team, you can see the patterns are there," Amorim added.
"We didn't lose so many points, we dropped two to Lazio and Juventus away, so not everything is bad.

"Sometimes it looks like that, especially after recent results, but we have to see the balance. We won today against a good team that is doing well, but it is a different team, and sometimes we will have issues.
"It's a process, I think we should have more points, as against Juventus we weren't playing so well, but we were 30 seconds off getting three points.
"Even against Lazio, if you look at the balance of the game, I feel we deserved a little bit more."

1m9ymt7iknsn317sgev2gjguoq.title: Man Utd striker Sesko withdraws from Slovenia squad due to shin issue
1m9ymt7iknsn317sgev2gjguoq.subtitle: A shin injury troubled Benjamin Sesko at the end of last season, and a flare-up of the issue has ruled him out of Slovenia's upcoming games.
paragraphs: Manchester United have confirmed striker Benjamin Sesko must undergo tests after withdrawing from the Slovenia squad with a shin injury.
Sesko was a notable absentee as United drew 1-1 with Fulham on Sunday, with Matheus Cunha's deflected strike salvaging a point for the Red Devils following Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal.
Having joined from RB Leipzig in a £74m deal last August, Sesko scored 12 goals in 32 appearances across all competitions last term.
That tally was only matched by Bryan Mbeumo among his Red Devils team-mates, despite 13 of Sesko's outings coming from the bench.
The 23-year-old missed the final few games of 2025-26, however, as well as United's entire pre-season campaign, with a shin problem.
Sesko has played six times for Michael Carrick's side this season, scoring twice, though he has only started twice – against Sabah in the Champions League and Brighton in the EFL Cup.
In the aftermath of last week's cup defeat to Brighton, Carrick revealed that the same issue was bothering Sesko again, and he has now withdrawn from Slovenia's squad.
Sesko was initially named in Bostjan Cesar's party for Nations League fixtures against Scotland – who they will face home and away – plus North Macedonia and Switzerland.
In a medical update released on Monday, United said: "Benjamin will undergo tests this week before defining his individual recovery plan."
Sesko has almost three weeks of recovery time if he is to feature in United's next Premier League game, against bottom club Tottenham on October 10.
They also face Leeds United, Bournemouth and Chelsea in the league next month, having made their joint-worst start to a Premier League season through five matchdays (also five points in 2014-15).

1oo6jjpc45ake1uj9k7ei6gwnd.title: Colwill expects Chelsea to be better after international break
1oo6jjpc45ake1uj9k7ei6gwnd.subtitle: Chelsea's strong start to the season fizzled out before the international break, but Levi Colwill is confident they can improve after it.
paragraphs: Levi Colwill has backed Chelsea to come out on the other side of the international break "flying".
Chelsea made a strong start to life under Xabi Alonso, winning four of their first five matches across all competitions (L1).

However, having had to come from behind to draw 2-2 with high-flying Hull City, the Blues were then thrashed 3-0 by Brentford in their final match before the extended international break to leave them winless in three league games.
Chelsea have already lost more Premier League matches in 2026 (11) than they did in the entirety of 2025 (10).

Alonso became only the sixth Premier League boss to see his side concede at least two goals in each of his first five games, after Mick McCarthy, Sammy Lee, Terry Connor, Slavisa Jokanovic, and Scott Parker.

And Chelsea's defensive woes have been highlighted on multiple occasions, even before Alonso's appointment; since the start of last season, they have conceded 23 Premier League goals from non-penalty set-pieces, now the joint-most of any side, along with Bournemouth.
Colwill admitted the start of the season was not what Chelsea expected, but he wants to use the extended international break to get back on track.
"[There have been] some good bits, some other not so good bits," he said, as quoted by Chelsea's website.
"Luckily, we've got a while now to try and improve.
"Hopefully, we will come out the other side flying, pick up our play, and become a better team."
Chelsea return to action at home to Bournemouth on October 10.

1pdab9mi3roft1tudzxduqx8gf.title: Xavi promises 'intensity and passion' in new-look Netherlands approach
1pdab9mi3roft1tudzxduqx8gf.subtitle: Xavi will take charge of the Netherlands for the first time this international break, and he is preparing his team for a new approach.
paragraphs: Xavi has promised to bring "intensity, passion and a good rhythm" to the Netherlands' play as he prepares to take charge for the first time.
The Spaniard was named as the Oranje's head coach on a four-year deal after Ronald Koeman left in the wake of a disappointing World Cup campaign over the summer.
While the Netherlands enjoyed an unbeaten group stage, they fell at the first hurdle in the knockouts, losing on penalties to Morocco.
Xavi, a former World Cup winner with Spain, will face Germany in his first game in charge in Amsterdam on Thursday, as the Netherlands kick off their Nations League campaign.

Koeman was criticised at times for taking a defensive approach with his tactics, and while Xavi did not give away too many hints about his approach, he outlined what he expects from his players on Monday.
"Everything is new ​for me and for the staff, so it will first be to get to know each other, ​know all the players, insist or convince them about our way to play," Xavi told reporters.
"We don't have too much time. But no excuses; every coach is in the same situation.

"I want to explain the values that ​we want from the squad. I want to show them that I'm open to them; I want ​to help them. I want to enjoy the process with them. We want to create a family; we want ‌to ⁠create a big group.
"The players must come to the national team with happiness, but at the end, the main goal is to win.

"You cannot promise results, but ​we will work ⁠for results. I can promise that we will play with intensity, with passion, with a good rhythm, trying to be competitive and trying to ​take the initiative in the game. This is for sure.
"There's going ​to be ⁠a different way of playing. I don't want to compare, and I don't want to talk about the past. I respect Ronald a lot. But I'm focused on the present."
Virgil van Dijk will remain the Netherlands' captain, having revealed on Sunday that he plans to keep representing his national team until Euro 2028.
"It ​was a really good meeting," Xavi said of meeting Van Dijk in Liverpool to discuss his Netherlands future.
"He was very honest. He has the capacity to continue. He's a good leader. He's positive, ​he's motivated. He's ready to be the leader."

1qjt6hutsp8xs131lm5v95llkq.title: Palmer and Rice withdraw from England squad as Gibbs-White, Garner come in
1qjt6hutsp8xs131lm5v95llkq.subtitle: Thomas Tuchel will be without Declan Rice, Cole Palmer and Marcus Rashford for England's upcoming Nations League fixtures.
paragraphs: Cole Palmer and Declan Rice are part of a quintet of players who have withdrawn from England duty.
Palmer, who missed out on England's World Cup squad, was selected by Thomas Tuchel for the Three Lions' upcoming Nations League matches.
He has already registered four Premier League goal involvements this season (two goals, two assists).
However, the Chelsea playmaker has now opted out of the squad as he nurses an injury.
It is the same case for Rice, Marcus Rashford, Tino Livramento and Kobbie Mainoo.
Tuchel has called up Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner as replacements.
No player has scored more Premier League goals in 2026 than Nottingham Forest attacker Gibbs-White (13, level with Erling Haaland).

Garner, meanwhile, made his England debut during the March international window, and impressed against Uruguay and Japan, but the Everton midfielder ultimately missed out on a call-up for the World Cup.
The pair will now get a chance to impress in fixtures against world champions Spain, with a double-header against Czechia following, either side of a clash with Croatia.

1qojeh2n1l0bn1lthi9ii0jc3a.subtitle: Jose Mourinho criticised Ortiz Arias after Real Madrid's loss to Atletico Madrid, but Claude Makelele says the referee was not to blame.
paragraphs: Ex-Real Madrid midfielder Claude Makelele did not hold back on his former team's performance in their derby defeat to Atletico Madrid, saying they had "no gameplan and no ideas."
Madrid slipped to a 2-1 loss against their cross-city rivals on Sunday, their second in the first seven games of their LaLiga campaign.
With defending champions Barcelona making a perfect start, Los Blancos are already six points off the title pace, and Makelele feels there are glaring issues in their side.

During Sunday's game, Madrid only managed eight shots and 0.3 expected goals, compared to Atleti's 18 attempts and 2.35 xG, though that latter figure was boosted by the penalty from which Alejandro Grimaldo opened the scoring early in the second half.

Dean Huijsen was sent off and conceded that spot-kick for denying Giuliano Simeone a clear goalscoring opportunity, though Madrid had been flat in attack even with 11 men on the pitch, only posting 0.16 xG and one shot on target in the first half.
And Makelele, who represented Madrid 145 times between 2000 and 2003, before working under Mourinho at Chelsea, was bemused by their lacklustre display.
"There is no understanding between the players, nor with the coach. Mourinho must talk to them," he told ESPN.
"The team is weak, there is no gameplan and no clear ideas. There is nothing. Nothing, nothing, nothing... Absolutely nothing. We must demand more from them."

In stark contrast to Madrid's stuttering performance, Atleti scored their second goal – via Jonathan David – at the end of an 18-pass move – the most for any goal scored by either team in a Madrid derby in LaLiga since at least 2005-06.

Afterwards, Mourinho said "the story of the game" was an inept refereeing performance from Ortiz Arias, arguing both Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have seen red for Atleti, the former for a high challenge on Federico Valverde and the latter for treading on Jude Bellingham.
Mourinho brought printed images of both incidents to his post-match press conference, prompting Atleti to hit back on social media, posting: "Stop referee harassment now."
But Makelele was not interested in playing the blame game, saying: "The problem is not the referee; there is an obvious deficiency in the team."
After the extended international break, Madrid host Villarreal in LaLiga on October 10, before visiting Roma in the Champions League four days later.

1swnm130vactq13ofzh6lz9vl9.title: Sunderland hand Le Fee new five-year contract
1swnm130vactq13ofzh6lz9vl9.subtitle: Having helped Sunderland qualify for the Europa League and scored their first European goal in 53 years, Enzo Le Fee has penned a new deal.
paragraphs: Sunderland's creative midfielder Enzo Le Fee has signed a new five-year contract with the club.
Le Fee joined the Black Cats on loan from Roma in January 2025, with that deal containing a purchase obligation if they were to be promoted from the Championship.
The Frenchman immediately assumed a key role under Regis Le Bris, starting in a 2-1 play-off final victory over Sheffield United, which led to him becoming a permanent Sunderland player for £19m.
And he has continued to shine in the Premier League, making 41 appearances in the competition while scoring six goals and providing seven assists.

His 13 goal involvements and 61 chances created are both team-high totals since the start of 2025-26, and those figures helped propel Sunderland to a seventh-place finish and Europa League qualification last term.
Last week, Le Fee scored from the penalty spot to secure a 1-0 victory over AZ at the Stadium of Light, in Sunderland's opening match in that competition.

That made him the Black Cats' first goalscorer in Europe since October 1973, when Micky Horswill scored their second goal in a 2-1 victory at home to Sporting CP in the Cup Winners' Cup, only for the Lisbon giants to recover in the return fixture and progress 3-2 on aggregate.
"I'm really happy to have signed a new contract with Sunderland," Le Fee told the club's website, having agreed fresh terms to run until 2031.
"From the moment I arrived, I've felt the passion of the supporters and the ambition of everyone at the club – I've loved my time here.
"We've achieved something special together over the past couple of seasons, but I believe this is just the beginning.
"I feel very settled here and I'm excited to continue developing, competing at the highest level and helping the club move forward.
"I'm very proud to wear the Sunderland shirt and I can't wait to see what we can achieve together in the years ahead."

Having lost 5-3 to Manchester City in a thrilling encounter prior to the international break, Sunderland have four points from five Premier League games this season, with Brighton their next opponents on October 10.

1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.title: Luis Enrique not taking Classique triumph for granted
1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.subtitle: Marquinhos struck the winner as Paris Saint-Germain overcame Marseille in Sunday's matchup between France's two most successful clubs.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique said Paris Saint-Germain can never take a win over Classique rivals Marseille for granted, after they battled to a 2-1 success at the Stade Velodrome.
Marquinhos' 74th-minute strike settled the contest as PSG claimed back-to-back Ligue 1 victories, having started their campaign with three winless games.
The Brazilian's goal came just two minutes after Angel Gomes got Marseille back on level terms, with that strike also coming hot on the heels of Ferran Torres' opener.
Marseille had captain Timothy Weah sent off shortly after going 2-1 down, with the United States international hauling Nuno Mendes down from behind while already on a yellow card.

PSG have now won 10 of their last 14 away Ligue 1 games against Marseille (D3 D1), though Nayef Aguerd missed a huge chance to snatch a point for OM deep into stoppage time, as he headed wide on the stretch.
And Luis Enrique says three points will never come easily for any visiting side at the Velodrome.
"It was the match we had planned for, with a lot of difficulties. Everyone said it would be easy, but playing at the Velodrome is not an easy thing," he told Ligue 1+.
"We tried to play, we created fewer chances in the first half because the opponent defended very well. In the second half, everything changed, we made a very good effort."

The result piles more pressure on Bruno Genesio, who is the first Marseille boss to lose four of his first five league games in charge of the club since the duo of Willy Kohut and Andre Gascard in 1938.

Marseille will spend the three-week international break 17th in the Ligue 1 table, with this the latest point into a season that they have sat in the relegation zone since 2011-12, when they were 20th with three points after six games and ultimately finished 10th.
But Luis Enrique expects them to come good eventually, saying: "Nothing was easy, we saw a very good OM team, with the way they defended. They have a great coach, I'm sure they will improve."
Genesio himself, however, admits Marseille's results have fallen well short of the required standard and has revealed he will hold talks with the club's hierarchy during the break.
"It's funny, everyone wishes me good luck. I'm a coach, so obviously I'm linked to the performances and results, especially at a club like OM," he said.
"This is insufficient, I assume my share of responsibility, as others will have to assume it too.
"I'm not there yet, I'm going to digest this defeat, talk to my staff, talk to my directors.
"Because I think – and I'm trying to weigh my words – that it's not normal for OM to be in this situation."
While PSG host Le Mans in their next Ligue 1 game on October 10, Marseille go to Troyes the following day.

1ur5y32ga6uu512tn6izb1ktkt.title: 'Stop referee harassment now' – Atleti hit back at Mourinho following derby comments
1ur5y32ga6uu512tn6izb1ktkt.subtitle: Jose Mourinho launched into a rant about refereeing standards following Real Madrid's defeat to Atletico Madrid, who have now hit back.
paragraphs: Atletico Madrid have hit back at Jose Mourinho following his rant about referee Ortiz Arias in the aftermath of their derby win over Real Madrid.
Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David were on target on Sunday as Los Colchoneros overcame their cross-city rivals 2-1 at the Estadio Metropolitano.
The victory lifted Diego Simeone's side to second in LaLiga, five points behind leaders Barcelona, going into the three-week international break, with Los Blancos a point further back in fourth.

But their win was not without controversy, as Madrid had centre-back Dean Huijsen sent off for denying Giuliano Simeone a clear goalscoring opportunity, and Mourinho felt Atleti were fortunate to keep all 11 men on the pitch.
Lee Kang-In avoided punishment for a high challenge that caught Federico Valverde on his ankle, leaving the Uruguay international requiring medical tests.
Cristian Romero, meanwhile, was only cautioned for what Madrid believed was a stamp on Jude Bellingham's knee, despite Arias being sent to the VAR monitor to check the incident.

Mourinho appeared at his post-match press conference with printed images of both incidents, saying they were both "clear red cards" and arguing Arias was not equipped to handle the pressure of such a big game.
Simeone subsequently said it was important that referees are protected and told his Madrid counterpart: "Not everything goes, even for Mourinho."
And on Monday, Atleti's club account on X posted an image of Mourinho discussing the incidents at his press conference, along with the caption: "Stop referee harassment now."
Atleti have only lost one of the last eight derbies between the teams in LaLiga (W3 D4), winning four of the last six meetings to take place at the Metropolitano (D1 L1).
Los Colchoneros have also won seven straight home games against teams from the Community of Madrid, the longest such winning streak in their history.

1vti29e1jbzts1xjheqztrgw5c.title: Aguirre returns to Spain with LaLiga strugglers Valencia
1vti29e1jbzts1xjheqztrgw5c.subtitle: After spending two years away from LaLiga, Javier Aguirre is back in Spain, being tasked with trying to turn Valencia's fortunes around.
paragraphs: Javier Aguirre has been appointed as the new head coach of Valencia on a contract that will run until the end of the campaign.
Aguirre arrives at the Estadio de Mestalla following a two-year stint in charge of Mexico, who he led to the round of 16 at this summer's World Cup.
The 67-year-old's deal contains an option for him to remain at the helm for a second season in Valencia, who have made a dismal start to 2026-27.
Valencia are 19th in LaLiga with four points from their opening seven games, with Carlos Corberan sacked just two months after extending his deal until 2028.
Oscar Sanchez took interim charge and helped Valencia to their first win of the season against Alaves, before overseeing a 3-2 defeat to Real Sociedad last Sunday.
Aguirre arrives with plenty of experience. He has managed 468 matches in LaLiga, the fifth-highest total of any foreign coach in the history of the competition.

The Mexican will be the fourth foreign manager to coach seven different teams in LaLiga, after Roque Olsen (seven), Ferdinand Daucik (nine), and Marcel Domingo (11), having previously taken charge of Osasuna, Atletico Madrid, Real Zaragoza, Espanyol, Leganes and Mallorca.
Aguirre's arrival comes after he announced ahead of this summer's World Cup that he would be leaving Mexico, with Rafael Marquez coming in to take over.
He was unable to end Mexico's wait for a first quarter-final appearance since 1986, after they were beaten 3-2 by 10-man England on home soil.

The defeat was Mexico's first at the Azteca in a competitive match for 13 years, since losing to Honduras in a qualifier for the 2014 World Cup, while it was the first time they had conceded three goals at the venue since a 4-3 triumph over Brazil in August 1999.
But Aguirre will now turn his attention back to club football, having last been in charge of Mallorca, who he helped avoid relegation from LaLiga in 2021-22.
Aguirre also led Mallorca to the Copa del Rey final in 2024, but they were beaten on penalties by Athletic Club before he parted ways with the club that summer.
His first home game in charge will come against Athletic on October 17, but he will make his bow for Valencia six days earlier, away to Racing de Santander.

1wzp4sylqp3g14dctwhmxr2c7.title: Martinez: Argentina must forget World Cup heartache and celebrate Messi
1wzp4sylqp3g14dctwhmxr2c7.subtitle: Lionel Messi will make his farewell appearance for Argentina during the international break, before he steps away from the Albiceleste.
paragraphs: Lisandro Martinez says Argentina's players are determined to put their World Cup final heartache behind them and savour Lionel Messi's international send-off next month.

The Albiceleste could have become the first back-to-back winners of FIFA's showpiece tournament since Brazil in 1958 and 1962, after Messi inspired them to a final appearance in North America this summer.
However, Enzo Fernandez's red card proved costly as Spain beat them 1-0 in extra time, with Ferran Torres scoring the all-important goal.

Argentina have now been World Cup runners-up four times (also in 1930, 1990 and 2014), the joint-most of any nation alongside West Germany/Germany, and they became the first team to not attempt a single shot in regulation time of a World Cup final.
But Manchester United defender Martinez says the time has come for Lionel Scaloni's side to put that defeat behind them, as they prepare to say goodbye to a legend.
Having announced his decision to retire from international football following the World Cup, Messi will make a farewell appearance at a friendly against Benin on October 5.

Bolivia and Burkina Faso will be Argentina's opponents before that match, which will see members of the 2022 World Cup-winning squad come together for a celebration of Messi's career at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.
"There's a lot of pain, preferably we don't remember it, but we must also highlight the tremendous effort we made throughout the tournament," Martinez told ESPN Argentina.
"Without a doubt, we had a great World Cup, but it hurts us all to have lost the final.
"Now we are here, back in our country, and we are going to enjoy ourselves."

Messi has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina, leading his country's all-time charts in both categories, with his last strike coming in their dramatic World Cup round-of-16 victory over Egypt this summer.
No player has directly contributed to more goals at the World Cup on record (since 1966) than Messi (33 – 21 goals and 12 assists), who has also featured in the most games at the finals (34).

Messi's 12 assists in the competition are also the most of any player, four more than the great Diego Maradona (eight), while only Kylian Mbappe (22 goals) has netted more often, though Messi was the first to surpass Miroslav Klose's previous record of 16 goals this year.

1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.title: Spalletti relieved to see Juventus banish Sassuolo 'doubts' against Atalanta
1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.subtitle: Having seen their unbeaten Serie A start halted by Sassuolo on matchday four, Juventus bounced back with an impressive win over Atalanta.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti admitted Juventus' defeat to Sassuolo last week had created doubt in the Bianconeri's ranks, and he was delighted to see them banish that feeling by beating Atalanta.
Juve suffered their first defeat of the Serie A campaign on matchday four, conceding a stoppage-time winner to Vasilije Adzic in a 3-2 loss to Sassuolo.
However, they bounced back in style on Sunday with a 2-0 success against Atalanta and their former head coach Maurizio Sarri, with Francisco Conceicao and Bremer on target.

Juve have now won three of their first five games of a Serie A season while keeping a clean sheet in each victory for the first time since 2017-18, when they went on to win the Scudetto under Massimiliano Allegri.
And with a three-week international break now on the horizon, Spalletti was relieved to see his team cast aside the negativity of their previous Serie A outing.
He told Sky Sport Italia: "There was a moment when we were forced to defend, then we had to change something and, from there, we got back on track and played on an equal footing in the second half.
"We can certainly get better with the start of our actions and in the build-up. We could have hurt Atalanta more.
"But that's okay, also because the defeat against Sassuolo had created some doubts for us."

Spalletti also reserved particular praise for Randal Kolo Muani, whose performances he criticised last month, despite the Frenchman missing a big one-v-one chance with an expected goals (xG) value of 0.35 – the highest of any shot in the match.
"He had a really good game. I was disappointed when he popped up one-on-one with the goalkeeper because he deserved to score," Spalletti said of Kolo Muani.
"But he was still very happy at the end and we joked about it. We're all happy because now we can recover some of our strong players, who would have been useful to us recently."
While Juve are seventh in the table going into the break with 10 points on the board, Atalanta are four points worse off in 11th.
Sarri – a Scudetto winner in his only season in charge of Juventus in 2019-20 – has now lost nine Serie A matches against the Bianconeri, his joint-most against any club (also Roma).
Though La Dea have now lost three straight games, Sarri insists there is no crisis brewing in Bergamo.
"I don't think so, the first three games were a lower level of performance, but we have been improving," he said.
"This team needs to have more character, to light up that fire in its soul. This is a side with certain capabilities and we need to access them."

And with a three-week international break now on the horizon, Spalletti was relieved to see his team cast aside the negativity of their previous Serie A outing.

He told Sky Sport Italia: "There was a moment when we were forced to defend, then we had to change something and, from there, we got back on track and played on an equal footing in the second half. 

"We can certainly get better with the start of our actions and in the build-up. We could have hurt Atalanta more. 

"But that's okay, also because the defeat against Sassuolo had created some doubts for us."

Spalletti also reserved particular praise for Randal Kolo Muani, whose performances he criticised last month, despite the Frenchman missing a big one-v-one chance with an expected goals (xG) value of 0.35 – the highest of any shot in the match.

"He had a really good game. I was disappointed when he popped up one-on-one with the goalkeeper because he deserved to score," Spalletti said of Kolo Muani.

"But he was still very happy at the end and we joked about it. We're all happy because now we can recover some of our strong players, who would have been useful to us recently."

While Juve are seventh in the table going into the break with 10 points on the board, Atalanta are four points worse off in 11th. 

Sarri – a Scudetto winner in his only season in charge of Juventus in 2019-20 – has now lost nine Serie A matches against the Bianconeri, his joint-most against any club (also Roma).

Though La Dea have now lost three straight games, Sarri insists there is no crisis brewing in Bergamo.

"I don't think so, the first three games were a lower level of performance, but we have been improving," he said. 

"This team needs to have more character, to light up that fire in its soul. This is a side with certain capabilities and we need to access them."

2208B0258C566247C168DE0E73060A38.title: The FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 5’s Best XI includes Brobbey, Manzambi, Groß and Semenyo
2208B0258C566247C168DE0E73060A38.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 5’s Best XI includes Brobbey, Manzambi, Groß and SemenyoShareMatchday 5 of the Premier League season is done and dusted, with Manchester City establishing a three-point advantage at the top of the table courtesy of Arsenal’s defeat against Brighton.
It will be a sad time when Alisson finally leaves Liverpool, especially as he is still more than capable of producing excellent displays like the one against Bournemouth.

The Brazilian made two saves during the game, including an impressive effort to prevent Evanilson from opening the scoring in the first half – a shot worth 0.78 xGOT. That was his third Premier League clean sheet in a row.
The Barcelona loanee makes it into FotMob’s Team of the Week for the second time in three weeks thanks to another solid display.

Araújo wasn’t quite at his best in the final third, yet the right-back made five defensive contributions including two tackles, while also registering six recoveries throughout the game. He even won 86% of his aerial duels and played a massive part in Liverpool keeping that clean sheet for Alisson.
Everton kept their fifth clean sheet across seven matches in all competitions against Ipswich at the weekend and James Tarkowski played a big part in the 1-0 win.
The defender provided the assist for Everton’s only goal while also notching up 12 defensive contributions throughout the 90 minutes.

Seven of those were clearances, and Tarkowski was also a rock when it came to duels, winning 100% of his ground and 83% of his aerial duels in the contest. He was certainly more than deserving of his 8.5 rating.
Brentford’s 3-0 victory over Chelsea was arguably the result of Matchday 5 and Jannik Schuster was rock solid at the heart of the defence.

With 16, the Austrian centre-back registered the most defensive contributions in the game, and he even chipped in at the other end of the pitch, grabbing an assist and making three passes into the final third.
Aged just 20, Schuster could be the future of Brentford’s defence over the next few years.
Jay Dasilva’s thumping effort against Nottingham Forest gave Coventry their first Premier League win since 2001 and he fully deserves his spot in the Team of the Week.

The left-back was a menace on the left flank, succeeding with 100% of his dribble attempts while also making six passes into the final third. Frank Lampard will be expecting more of the same when domestic action returns next month.
Chema Andrés provided an assist on his Premier League debut last weekend, but he went one better against Arsenal, netting the third goal in Brighton’s victory against the champions.
It was a splendid performance by the midfielder who looked equally adept whether he was defending or trying to make things happen in the final third against the Gunners.
Five passes into the final third, nine defensive contributions, and winning five out of five aerial duels ensure he makes his FotMob Team of the Week debut.
Pascal Groß is ageing like a fine wine, isn’t he? The German midfielder covered the most ground against Arsenal (12.6 km), despite being the oldest player on the pitch.
He not only scored, but provided an assist during the contest, and also made eight passes into the final third.
Groß added five defensive contributions and was well deserving of making the Team of the Week for the second consecutive matchday.
