o0w0ojavvskfzvw31lgmcrhf.title: Robertson urges struggling Spurs to forget about last two seasons
o0w0ojavvskfzvw31lgmcrhf.subtitle: Tottenham are bottom of the Premier League after five games, having only escaped relegation by two points on the final day of last season.
paragraphs: Andy Robertson says Tottenham's players must forget about their struggles over the last couple of seasons if they are to climb the Premier League table.

Spurs will spend the international break bottom of the Premier League with just two points on the board, with this the first time they have propped up the table at least five games into a season since 2008-09.

Roberto De Zerbi's side did at least end their goalless start to the campaign against Aston Villa on Saturday, but after going down 3-2, they have lost 50 of their 141 Premier League games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
In just seven years at the venue, they have suffered as many Premier League defeats as rivals Arsenal have suffered in 382 matches at the Emirates Stadium, which opened 20 years ago.
Spurs finished 17th in both 2024-25 and 2025-26, narrowly avoiding relegation in the latter of those seasons as they finished two points clear of West Ham on the final matchday.

They then spent over £300m on new players in the summer transfer window, but Robertson believes there is still a hangover from their disappointing recent seasons, which he and his fellow new arrivals can help to overcome.
"They're starting this journey. They've had a couple of really tough seasons in terms of finishes in the league," Robertson said in an appearance on The Overlaps' Stick to Football podcast.
"They've had to go into the market, they've spent a bit of money, but I do believe Tottenham are now starting a journey.

"Now, I don't know how far that journey can go, nobody does, but the determination in that group... you can see last season hurt them a lot. And maybe we're still guilty of carrying that weight of last season on our shoulders.

"That's the message of the manager, first and foremost. And also, that falls on me, and the other new players, if we need to forget. We need to now try and get Tottenham back to where we believe they belong. The fans are still carrying it as well and you don't blame them. They've been through such a tough time."
Robertson joined Tottenham on a free transfer after nine years with Liverpool, who he helped to win two Premier League titles, one FA Cup and two EFL Cups.
And when Robertson became aware his contract at Anfield would not be renewed, he immediately viewed Spurs as the most attractive destination available to him.
"I spoke directly to the manager. We had a couple of video calls over the summer. He's super ambitious, you can tell that as a manager," Robertson said of his initial conversations with De Zerbi.
"He wants to be able to win trophies. But he also knows that we need to start showing it sooner rather than later.
"It was always going to be Tottenham, even from January, as long as they stayed up. I ended up getting invested in Tottenham games.
"I was watching Tottenham thinking, 'come on', especially when De Zerbi came in. I was fully confident; I was really happy with how much Spurs wanted me."

Spurs' next Premier League game is against Manchester United at Old Trafford on October 10, with the Red Devils making their joint-worst start to a Premier League season after five matches (five points, level with 2014-15).

o7k6ie5pw9vm19jmzjjysrlqa.title: 'When he calls, you can't say no' – Ebnoutalib credits Klopp for choice to represent Germany
o7k6ie5pw9vm19jmzjjysrlqa.subtitle: Younes Ebnoutalib was eligible to represent either Germany or Morocco, and he says talks with Jurgen Klopp made his mind up.
paragraphs: Eintracht Frankfurt forward Younes Ebnoutalib has highlighted the role Jurgen Klopp played in his choice to represent Germany over Morocco, saying: "When he calls, you can't say no."

Klopp has named a larger, 44-man squad for his first international break in charge of Germany, who face the Netherlands in their Nations League opener on Thursday, before taking on Greece twice, either side of a home clash with Serbia.
Sixteen of them are uncapped as Klopp looks to familiarise himself with as many players as possible, with 23-year-old attacker Ebnoutalib among them.
Having joined Eintracht from Elversberg in a €10m deal in January, Ebnoutalib has made a superb start to this season, scoring four goals in as many Bundesliga games.

Only Patrik Schick, Phillip Tietz, Michael Olise and Yuito Suzuki can match that tally, with Ebnoutalib finding the net with all but one of his shots on target (five, from 11 total attempts) and overperforming his figure of 2.85 expected goals (xG).
Ebnoutalib represented Morocco at youth level, but talks with Jurgen Klopp left him in no doubt as to where his international future lay.
"I am very, very proud. There were also talks with Morocco, but they weren't as intense as with Jurgen," Ebnoutalib said.
"I'm just proud. You have to say, he is one of the best coaches in the world. And when he calls, you can't say no.
"The impression is very positive. He is, of course, someone who brings a great deal of experience and already has a certain presence because of what he has achieved over the years.
"So, naturally, you have a great deal of respect for him. But he was very nice and very likeable in the conversations.
"He is already very well known for the way he wants to play football, with high pressing, with a lot of energy and power. He has already fired us up.
"I think that's what he is known for, that he is very good at reaching people and getting them on board. He has certainly got us in the right mindset."

Klopp has overseen 1,080 matches across his managerial career, winning 588 of those (D256 L236). His 431 games in charge of Liverpool are the third-most by a manager in the club's history, behind Bill Shankly's 799 and Bob Paisley's 523.

Klopp's 334 Premier League games with the Reds, who won the title under him in 2019-20, are also the fifth-most with a single club in the history of the competition, after Arsene Wenger with Arsenal (828), Alex Ferguson with Manchester United (810), David Moyes with Everton (488) and Pep Guardiola with Manchester City (380).

Defender Philipp Treu is another player hoping to make his senior Germany debut in the coming days, with three of his Freiburg team-mates also called up following their run to the Europa League final last season.
"It's definitely something where you say, 'Hey, it's cool that I can now train under Jurgen Klopp'," Treu said of working with Klopp.
"And that's why I'm just looking forward to being on the pitch with him later, soaking it all in, and just giving it my all."

qoth7vtxk05i1dxyoa71q6hza.title: Kolo Muani not facing spell out after hand surgery
qoth7vtxk05i1dxyoa71q6hza.subtitle: Randal Kolo Muani has undergone surgery on a fractured finger on his right hand, but he will not miss any time for Juventus.
paragraphs: Juventus have confirmed Randal Kolo Muani will remain available for selection after undergoing surgery on a fractured finger.
Kolo Muani played 89 minutes on Saturday as the Bianconeri returned to winning ways in Serie A, beating Atalanta 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium.
He played on despite sustaining an injury to his right hand, and though the issue required surgery, reports in Italy said he would return to training with Juve within a couple of days.
A statement released on Juve's website said: "During the first half of Sunday's match against Atalanta, Randal Kolo Muani sustained an injury to the fifth finger of his right hand.
"Tests carried out after the match revealed a fracture of the proximal phalanx, making osteosynthesis surgery necessary.
"The operation, performed this afternoon by Dr Loris Pegoli, was completely successful and the player will remain available for selection."
Kolo Muani has appeared in all six of the Bianconeri's matches in all competitions this season, starting five of those and recording one goal and two assists in 468 minutes.

He was not selected in Zinedine Zidane's first France squad ahead of their Nations League fixtures against Turkiye, Belgium and Italy, so will continue training with his club ahead of Juve facing Cagliari on October 11.

vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.title: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC: Dreyer strikes late to deny Messi and co.
vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.subtitle: Inter Miami's recent struggles continued as they played out yet another draw in MLS, losing more ground on the Eastern Conference leaders.
paragraphs: Anders Dreyer netted a late equaliser to earn San Diego FC a 2-2 draw with Inter Miami, who were held to a fourth straight stalemate despite Lionel Messi's free-kick.

Dreyer opened the scoring early on, but Miami turned the game on its head, with Messi and Luis Suarez both hitting the back of the net, only for San Diego's striker to complete his brace with eight minutes remaining at Nu Stadium.

San Diego's 12th-minute opener came out of nowhere as Jeppe Tverskov slotted a perfectly weighted throughball in behind for Dreyer, who charged in behind Miami's defense from the halfway line before dinking a lovely shot over Dayne St. Clair.
Twelve minutes later, Miami were back on level terms. Messi's free-kick looked to be more of a cross as it floated towards the far post, but it missed everyone in the middle and snuck in.

German Berterame's curler was cleared in front of the line by the retreating Ian Murphy, but San Diego could not clear their lines as Yannick Bright picked out Messi, whose first-time shot was kept out by CJ dos Santos.
Marcus Ingvartsen had a goal disallowed shortly after at the other end for an offside in the build-up, while Dos Santos punched away an awkward strike from Suarez.
But the Uruguayan soon got his goal in the 74th minute, lifting over Dos Santos from a tight angle to find the far corner.
Miami's lead only lasted eight minutes, though, with Dreyer again timing his run to perfection to meet a Tverskov pass, and a rooted St. Clair could not get a hand to it.

Messi had the chance to win it in stoppage time, bending a low shot through the crowded box, but Dos Santos got down to keep it out despite seeing it late, meaning Miami sit 11 points behind Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC.
Messi makes more history despite Miami's frustrations
While Miami are unbeaten in their last five matches, they have drawn each of the last four, having held the lead in three of those.

But Messi has played his part in trying to get Miami back to winning ways, and netted his 101st goal for the Herons in total, while extending his lead in the Golden Boot race, as it was his 20th in MLS this season.
That means he is now just the second player in the league's history to score 20+ goals in three straight seasons, after Los Angeles FC's Denis Bouanga (2023-2025).
Messi finished the match with 10 shots – Miami had 19 overall – with five of those on target, while he also led the metrics for touches in the opposition box (14) and chances created (three).
But Dreyer ensured Messi would not end up on the winning side on Sunday, as he netted his 11th goal in MLS this term, more than any other San Diego player.
It was a vital point for San Diego, who halted a three-game losing streak and responded well to their 5-0 thumping at the hands of the Philadelphia Union.

Messi finished the match with 10 shots – Miami had 19 overall – with five of those on target, while he also led the metrics for touches in the opposition box (14) and chances created (three).

But Dreyer ensured Messi would not end up on the winning side on Sunday, as he netted his 11th goal in MLS this term, more than any other San Diego player.

It was a vital point for San Diego, who halted a three-game losing streak and responded well to their 5-0 thumping at the hands of the Philadelphia Union.

vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.title: Wirtz 'the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt' against Bournemouth, claims Carragher
vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.subtitle: Florian Wirtz struggled to make an impact against Bournemouth, and Jamie Carragher has questioned his starting place going forward.
paragraphs: Jamie Carragher believes Florian Wirtz must be dropped for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after the international break, claiming his performance against Bournemouth was the "poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt".
Liverpool edged to a 1-0 victory over Bournemouth, giving Andoni Iraola a winning return to Vitality Stadium thanks to Alexander Isak's second-half goal.
Iraola is the first manager to remain unbeaten in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool (W2 D3) since Joe Fagan in September 1983.
However, Wirtz came under fire for his performance on the south coast as he struggled to make an impact.
He finished the match with a team-low 70.3% passing accuracy (completing 26 of 37 passes), had 53 touches, and just two off-target shots, though he did create a joint-game-high three chances.
Only Ronald Araujo (24) lost possession more often than the German (16).
And Carragher was far from impressed by Wirtz's showing, claiming that Iraola needs to think about leaving him out of the side if they want to improve their results.
"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," said Carragher on the bonus Jamie Carragher Podcast.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy; he keeps possession. There's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.
"But the reason I worry is: I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.
"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley, and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game, it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you.
"It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.

"And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No. 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player; I don't.
"I think going forward, Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team.
"Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home; for me, he can't be in the team."
Wirtz has been called up in Jurgen Klopp's Germany squad for the upcoming Nations League.
Klopp – the former Liverpool manager – has named two squads, with Wirtz getting a rest before being in contention for their final two games of the international break against Serbia and Greece.
"The one hope for Liverpool supporters now is Jurgen Klopp is the Germany manager," Carragher added.

"Wirtz goes away with the Germany team for three weeks, and he's obviously one of the best players in Germany; that's how they see him. Can Jurgen Klopp sprinkle a bit of stardust on him in that position?

"Jurgen is one of the greatest managers in the world; we know that. And what he gets out of players is probably more than most managers because of the nature of his personality, and fingers crossed something can happen for him.

"There's a scenario there that Jurgen Klopp and Germany have a great international window, he gets loads of goals, assists and comes back on a high. Manchester City's the next game; he impacts that, all is forgotten, all is forgiven. There's a potential turnaround there.
"I would love that to happen. I'd love him to be the match-winner against Manchester City."
Liverpool, who sit sixth in the Premier League table on nine points after an unbeaten start, return to action on October 11 against leaders Manchester City.
